 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 16122020 at about 1.30 p.m., the Petitioner was sitting on the scooter bearing No.KA02JE5039 which was parked by the side of the road, at that time,
one Hyundai Xcent car bearing Regn. No.KA03AE8357 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the parked scooter and caused the accident.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital wherein, he was treated as an inpatient.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was studying in II PUC.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending Hyundai Xcent car and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the Hyundai Xcent car and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.2 remained absent.

Hence,
he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared before the court through its counsel and filed objections to the main petition.
In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.1, it denied the age, education of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Hyundai Xcent car.

Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses Nitin.S vs The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81356053/
2 incurred for the medical treatment.

sentences.text: Further, it contended that at the time of alleged accident, the offending vehicle was plied without valid permit and fitness certificate.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 16.12.2020 at about 1.30 p.m. on 3rd Main Road, near Raghavendra Auto Mobile,
Rajajinagar Industrial Town, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Hyundai Xcent car bearing No. KA53MB6917?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award ?

5. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and also examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C as P.W.2 and got marked 28 documents as per Ex.P1 to P 28 and closed his side evidence.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 did not choose to lead any oral or documentary evidence 6. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents and upon perusal of the written arguments filed by the Learned counsel for the Petitioner and depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record.

My answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 7. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Motor Vehicle accident that occurred on 16122020 at about 1.30 p.m., when he was sitting on the scooter bearing No.KA02JE5039, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Hyundai Xcent car bearing Regn.No. KA03AE8357.
8.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Hyundai Xcent car.

9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and he also examined one witness Dr.Chidanand K.J.C as P.W.2 and got marked 28 documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P28.
P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in his chiefaffidavit.

Ex.P.7 is the Discharge summary and Ex.P.8 and 9 are the Outpatient records,
Ex.P.10 and 11 are the Admission Fee Receipts, Ex.P.12 is the Medical bills, Ex.P.13 is the Prescriptions, Ex.P.14 and 15 are the Aadhar card and ID card.

10. Upon going through Ex.P1, it shows that on the complaint lodged by the Petitioner before Magadi Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of the Hyundai Xcent car bearing Reg.No.KA 03AE8357 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 of IPC read with Section 134(A&B), 187 of MV Act.
Ex.P.2 is the Complaint.
Ex.P3 is the Spot Mahazar along with sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P4 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.
Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate issued by Sanjay Gandhi hospital.

Ex.P6 is the Certified copy of the charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Magadi Road Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending Hyundai Xcent car for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC read with Section 134(A&B), 187 of IMV Act.

1. Abrasion over left leg region.
Swelling & tenderness over left leg.

Xray shows fracture of left Proximal Tibia.
As per the opinion of the Doctor, the injury is grievous in nature.
13. Ex.P7 is the Discharge summary which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient on 16122020 and discharged on 28122020.
Ex.P8 and 9 are Outpatient records.
14. Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.Chidanand as P.W.2 and he also reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
15. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1 has cross examined the P.W.1.
In the crossexamination P.W.1 has denied the suggestions and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the petitioner.

16. Though the Respondent No.1 had taken contention that the accident does not caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, they did not lead any evidence to substantiate their contentions.
Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Charge sheet against the driver of the offending Hyundai Xcent car.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Hyundai Xcent car and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 in the 'Affirmative'.

17. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Hyundai Xcent car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
18. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 18 years.

Further, in the Aadhar card i.e.,
Ex.P14, the date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as 04022003.
The accident took place on 16122020.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 17 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
19. It is stated in the petition that the Petitioner is a student.
Further in the petition, the Petitioner has also mentioned that he is studying in II PUC, KLE College, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru.
Further, in the evidence of PW.1 he also deposed that at the time of accident, he was a student studying in II PUC in KLE College, Bengaluru.
Further he stated that after the accident due to the injuries and permanent disability, he discontinued his studies.
However, in the cross examination, he admitted that he has not produced document to show that he has discontinued his education.
Further PW.2 doctor has also admitted in his cross examination due to fracture, there is no problem to the education of the Petitioner.
Further, he admitted that the Petitioner is still a student and the fracture of the Petitioner is now united.
Further he deposed that he is not a treated doctor.
He has not conducted surgery to the fracture of the Petitioner.
But he is one among the doctors who has also given treatment to the Petitioner.
These evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 and also petition averments shows that the Petitioner is a student at the time of the accident and he is not doing any job along with his education.
Further, there is no problem for the education of the Petitioner.
Therefore, the question of loss of future income does not arise.

5 20.
However, Ex.P.5 i.e., Wound certificate shows that Petitioner had sustained abrasion over left leg region.
Swelling & tenderness over left leg.
Xray shows fracture of left Proximal Tibia.
According to the opinion of the doctor, the said injury is grievous in nature.
However PW.2 being the doctor has admitted that the said fracture is now united.
Further, Ex.P.12 i.e., 17 medical bills totally amounting to Rs.35,621/ shows that the Petitioner had incurred medical expenses to the extent of Rs.35,621/.
I have gone through the said medical bills which are acceptable.
Further, the Discharge summary i.e., Ex.P.7 shows that the Petitioner has admitted as an inpatient from 16.12.2020 to 28.12.2020 i.e., for 13 days in Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru.

Therefore, during the laid up period, the parents of the Petitioner might have look after the Petitioner and also might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

Therefore, by considering the pain and sufferings, medical expenses and expenses incurred for food and nourishment and other charges and also towards attendant, it is proper to grant global compensation of Rs.1,00,000/ under all heads.
21. Regarding Liability:
This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Hyundai Xcent car bearing No.KA03AE8357.
The Petition shows the Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Moreover, Respondent No.1 did not choose to lead evidence to prove its contention.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
22. Point No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No. 1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for global Compensation of Rs.1,00,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, since the same is meager one, the entire amount shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E Payment after his proper identification.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
